nodes.name: IF cleaning
nodes.procedure: The iron-foam (IF) substrates were cleaned with acetone and ethanol solution to remove residual fats.
nodes.source_text: The iron-foam (IF) substrates were cleaned with acetone and ethanol solution to remove residual fats.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal F-CoFe-PBA/IF
nodes.procedure: F-CoFe-PBA/IF nanocomposites were prepared by the hydrothermal method. In a typical experiment, a piece of 1 cm × 1 cm of iron-foam was exposed to 60 mL of an aqueous solution of 0.1 g of K₃[Co(CN)₆] and 0.1 g NH₄F, inside a Teflon lined autoclave at 90 °C for 24 h. After the hydrothermal treatment, the resulting modified foam was washed repeatedly with water and ethanol and then dried at 60 °C for 8 h.

nodes.name: Phosphorization F-Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF
nodes.procedure: The phosphorization of the F-CoFe-PBA/IF was carried out through a heat treatment (350 °C) under Ar atmosphere for 2 h. 1.0 g of sodium monophosphate powder was placed at the upstream side of a tube furnace, and a piece of F-CoFe-PBA/IF was located at the downstream side of the furnace. The F·Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF was obtained after naturally cooling to room temperature.
nodes.source_text: The phosphorization of the F-CoFe-PBA/IF was carried out through a heat treatment (350 °C) under Ar atmosphere for 2 h...

nodes.name: Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF synthesis
nodes.procedure: The synthesis of Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF was primarily used to compare properties with the F·Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF. Three pieces of clean IF were immersed into the K₃[Co(CN)₆] solution for 10 min and then maintained at 90 °C for 24 h. Next, the furnace was heated to 350 °C with a heating rate of 2 °C min⁻¹ under Ar flow and maintained at it for 2 h.

nodes.procedure: In order to explore the influence of the addition of cobalt on HER, the Fe₂P/IF has been synthesized. The phosphorization process is same with the F·Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1.0 M KOH three-electrode cell
nodes.source_text: As shown in Fig. 4a, IF, F-CoFe-PBA/IF and F·Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF exhibit significant hydrogen evolution electrocatalytic activities... When reaching the current density of 100 mA cm⁻², it only requires an overpotential of 151.8 mV. In addition, F-Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF could afford large current densities of 500, 1000, 2000 and 3000 mA cm⁻² at overpotentials of only 229.8, 260.5, 292.2 and 304.4 mV (Fig. 4b)... the slope value of F-Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF is 115.01 mV dec⁻¹... charge transfer resistance (R_ct) order is: F-Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF (4.13 Ω)... ECSA of F-Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF has a ECSA of 490 cm².

nodes.description: HER performance in 1.0 M KOH with 1 mM BaCl₂
nodes.source_text: As shown in Fig. 4e, a dramatic drop in the activity of the HER can be observed when the electrolyte containing a small amount of BaCl₂. To drive a current density of 500 mA cm⁻², the overpotential of F·Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF increases by 39.1 mV when tested in an electrolyte containing Ba²⁺. And the Tafel slope increases from 115.01 to 123.19 mV dec⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: Peaks at 44.60°, 64.67°, 82.35° indexed to iron foam (110), (200), (211) planes; additional peaks at 44.85°, 48.37° for Co₂P and 30.40°, 35.23°, 62.3°, 82.50° for Fe₂P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns are utilized to analyze the structural characterization of the as-prepared F·Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF and the result is shown in Fig. 1a. Where the peaks at 44.60°, 64.67°, 82.35° can be indexed to the iron foam (PDF no. 01-001-1262), which correspond to the (110), (200) and (211) planes, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Survey confirms presence of Fe, Co, P, O, F. Fe 2p peaks at 710.6/724.6 eV (oxidized Fe), 706.9/720.1 eV (Fe-P from Fe₂P); Co 2p at 778.9 eV (Co-P), 782.6/786.2 eV (Co ions); P 2p at 129.6 eV (P-Co/Fe), 134.1 eV (P-O); F 1s at 685.1 eV (ionic state).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Fe 2p XPS spectrum, it appears at 710.6 and 724.6 eV, that can be assigned to Fe 2p3/2 and Fe 2p1/2 components arising from Fe surface oxidation... For Co 2p spectrum (Fig. 1d), it shows three characteristic peaks at 778.9 eV (2p3/2), 782.6 eV (2p3/2) and 786.2 eV (2p3/2)... Fig. 1e is the high resolution of P 2p spectrum, which has two main peaks at 129.6 eV and 134.1 eV... As for F 1s in Fig. 1f, it exhibits a main peak (685.1 eV), indicating it exists in an ionic state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Polyhedral nanocube structure retained after phosphorization with increased surface roughness compared to precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2a-c is the image of F-Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF in different scales. It can be seen that the polyhedral structure is well retained without any collapse, suggesting the great structural strength and stability.

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous distribution of Fe (54.74 at%), Co (4.19 at%), F (0.82 at%), P (6.12 at%), O (34.17 at%).
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM mapping (Fig. 2d) and EDX data (Fig. S6) test results of F·Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF are fully confirmed the homogeneous distribution of Fe, Co, F, P and O elements, where the corresponding atomic percentages are 54.74%, 4.19%, 0.82%, 6.12% and 34.17%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Neat geometric structure with lattice fringes of 0.201 nm ((021) plane of Co₂P) and 0.254 nm ((200) plane of Fe₂P); polycrystalline nature confirmed by SAED rings.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, at the edge position, there are many distinct fringes with the lattice spacing of 0.201 nm and 0.254 nm, which are coincided with the (021) crystal plane of Co₂P and (200) crystal plane of Fe₂P₃, respectively... Fig. 3d is the SAED (selected area electron diffraction) diagram of F·Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF, the pattern of its multiple diffraction rings also shows its polycrystalline nature.

nodes.characterization_summary: Charge transfer resistance R_ct = 4.13 Ω, indicating fast charge transfer kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 4d, the charge transfer resistance (R_ct) order is: F-Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF (4.13 Ω) < F-CoFe-PBA/IF (23.81 Ω) < IF (31.52 Ω).

properties.description: Stability test at different current densities

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSA = 490 cm², 1.32 times higher than F-CoFe-PBA/IF (370.5 cm²) and 1.71 times higher than IF (285.25 cm²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The F-Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF has a ECSA of 490 cm², which is nearly 1.32 times than that of F-CoFe-PBA/IF (370.5 cm²) and 1.71 times that of IF (285.25 cm²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability test morphology shows nanocubes collapse to regular sheet structure after 10 h in 1 M KOH and to nanoparticles after 3600 s in 6 M KOH, but active sites maintained.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM also reflects these changes. As shown in Fig. 6a-b, SEM reveals that the nanocubes collapse and transform into a regular sheet structure. After stability test in 6 M KOH, the morphology is further changed to nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability XRD shows no obvious peak position changes (crystal structure retained) but weakened peak intensity possibly due to physical structure changes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Evidently, there are no obvious peak position changes in the XRD patterns, meaning that the crystal structures of F·Co₂P/Fe₂P/IF has been remained during the intense hydrogen evolution process. However, the intensity of peaks is weakened.
